places: Govandi, Mankhurd, Shivaji Nagar, Trombay, Deonar
note: MCAP flags M East as Mumbai’s most heat-stressed ward: over 40% of residents on surfaces above 35°C. Deonar dumping ground, Trombay industry, and dense informal housing stack heat, air, and service gaps on the same streets.

places: Kurla, Saki Naka, Chandivali, Mithi belt
note: Kurla sits on the Mithi floodplain under the airport approach. Waterlogging, traffic, and PM from construction and aviation hit the same dense neighbourhoods.

places: Bandra East, Khar East, Dharavi, Santacruz East
note: Dharavi plus the Western line yards: extreme crowding, few private toilets in pockets, and the Mithi/Mahim creek edge. Heat and services scores stay high even when the Arabian Sea breeze helps Bandra West next door.
Highest count of BMC-reported flooding hotspots (54). About 65% of the ward’s population lives within 250 m of a hotspot. Sion–Wadala drainage and the salt-pan edge flood when rain meets high tide.

places: Andheri East, Jogeshwari East, Vile Parle East, Sahar
note: Andheri East / Sahar: airport, SEEPZ, and the Western Express Highway. Night-time NO2 and PM stay elevated; monsoon flooding follows the old nallahs.
Malad / Malvani: fast-growing, high slum share, creek flooding on the west, and thin last-mile drainage.
Ghatkopar–Vikhroli. August 2026 landslide at Ghatkopar showed slope and informal-housing risk on top of waterlogging on the suburban line.
Dadar is a rail and stormwater pinch. IISER’s 2025 flood-vulnerability list keeps G North in the high band with Worli and Matunga.
Byculla has a BMC AQI station and dense traffic. Island-city flooding plus older housing stock.
Marine Lines / Kalbadevi: very small area, very high density, sea-facing drains that back up at tide.
Kandivali is on the 2025 high-flood list with Dahisar. Poisar river and creek outfalls.
Bhandup–Kanjurmarg: Eastern Express Highway, industrial pockets, Powai/Vihar edge.
Parel–Lalbaug: mill lands turned towers; stormwater still follows the old mill drains.
Chembur West / Mahul: refinery air, but fewer flood hotspots than M East.
Dahisar: northern creek, high-flood CFVI ward, hill-cut construction.
Worli and Lower Parel are on the CFVI high list (coastal outfalls, reclamation, high tide). New towers sit next to older chawls that still flood.
Dongri–Masjid: tiny footprint, dense old city, dock-edge drainage.
Goregaon / Aarey edge: mixed formal housing, some relief from the park, still monsoon flooding on the west.
Andheri West / Oshiwara: better services than K East, still monsoon nallah flooding.

places: Colaba, Cuffe Parade, Fort, Nariman Point
note: Colaba–Nariman Point is coastal and on the high-flood list, but heat and service strain are lower than the eastern suburbs. Reclamation and outfalls still fail at high tide.

places: Borivali East, Sanjay Gandhi National Park edge
note: Borivali East against SGNP: more green cover, lower heat, but creek flooding in spots.

places: Bandra West, Khar West, Santacruz West
note: Bandra–Khar West: sea breeze, stronger services, still waterlogging on Turner Road and Linking Road.
Mulund: higher ground, more planned layout, lowest composite exposure among the 24 wards in this index.

places: Malabar Hill, Walkeshwar, Grant Road, Tardeo
note: Malabar Hill / Walkeshwar: elevation and canopy cut heat and flood relative to the island city floor.
